subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother who stares unblinkingly at the escapees and realizes the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen, the archpriest of the Sea Mother, stares unblinkingly at the escapees.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father and Ploopploopeen’s daughter, whose relationship with her father is strained and whose devotion to the Deep Father is questioned.
source_quote: My daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg, who goes by Gloog, is a kuo-toan who disapproves of his sister Bloppblippodd’s actions and believes she has fallen prey to madness and disrespect for their ways.
source_quote: My name is Glooglugogg. Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways.

subject: Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is a village with two walls of nEttin g, a cave wall to the south, a Darklake to the north, and over a hundred houses with mud walls and ceilings made from unidentified dried vegetable matter.
source_quote: The tunnels eventually end up on the village's western side of about 500 kuo-toans. There is a wall made of nEttin g guarded by Kuo-toans... Between the two walls to the south is the cave wall. To the north, between the two nEttin g walls, is the Darklake. Between the walls of nEttin g, the cave wall, and the Darklake is the village. There are over a hundred houses of various sizes. Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.

subject: Darklake
fact: The Darklake is a body of water to the north of the two nEttin g walls, with docks, some of which have boats, and where groups of Kuo-Toans walk along its edge.
source_quote: The Darklake side has docks. Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty. Walking along the docks are groups of Kuo-Toans.

subject: Altar of the Sea Mother
fact: The altar of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden statue of a humanoid female, with its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed on with gut strands and emitting a rotting shellfish stench, with shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish piled at its feet and strung around its neck.
source_quote: Ploop stops in front of the sizeable nine-foot-tall statue. The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish. Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: Altar of Leemooggoogoon
fact: The altar of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father consists of a large hide stretched between two poles in the shape of a manta ray, with a dead splayed-out manta ray pinned to its center, two dead octopuses draped across the top with tentacles pinned and heads tied together and painted red and blue, reeking of decay and stained dark with blood.
source_quote: They sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father. It consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles. A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide. Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments. The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: nEttin g
fact: nEttin g is a material used to construct walls in Sloobludop, described as ineffective against determined invaders, and guarded by Kuo-toans who snap to attention when Ploop arrives.
source_quote: There is a wall made of nEttin g guarded by Kuo-toans... Thorin notes that the nEttin g isn’t an effective wall against a determined invader.

subject: gut strands
fact: Gut strands are used to lash the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish onto the statue of the Sea Mother, contributing to its overpowering stench.
source_quote: These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish.

subject: dried vegetable matter
fact: The ceilings of homes in Sloobludop are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter, a material common to all dwellings in the village.
source_quote: Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.

subject: red and blue pigments
fact: Red and blue pigments are used to paint the heads of the two dead octopuses on the altar of Leemooggoogoon, artfully arrayed and tied together.
source_quote: Their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.

subject: blood-stained altar
fact: The broad stone altar below the idol of Leemooggoogoon is stained dark with blood, indicating frequent ritual use.
source_quote: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: whip
fact: The whip is carried by the archpriest of the Sea Mother and accompanies him and the prisoners to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar is referenced as having explained that the Kuo-Toans walking along the docks are leader types responsible for ensuring the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.
source_quote: These leader types that Shuushar explained are responsible for ensuring that the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is skeptical of the Kuo-Toans’ cause, questions the existence of Leemooggoogoon, and initially sees no value in helping them until convinced by their customs.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders why they should bother. They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern... It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is the perfect form of offering, and he spits on the altar to demonstrate respect.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering. Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, having escaped prison and witnessed the death of a group member, finds purpose in helping the Kuo-Toans and declares that having something to focus on is less depressing than running.
source_quote: Man, we’ve been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing. We busted out of prison, and then what? Ran. We’re being chased, and we keep running. One of our group got killed by another of our group. Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is wary of raw rotting food, questions the effectiveness of nEttin g walls, and participates in spitting on the Sea Mother’s altar.
source_quote: Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food... Thorin notes that the nEttin g isn’t an effective wall against a determined invader... Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Kuo-toan monitor
fact: The kuo-toan monitor leads twelve kuo-toa to Ploopploopeen’s quarters and is admitted to oversee the transfer of prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: spitting on the Sea Mother’s altar
fact: Grygum and Thorin spit on the altar of the Sea Mother, which delights Ploopploopeen and confirms their respect for Kuo-Toan customs.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Kuo-toans sleeping with eyes open
fact: The escapees notice that many kuo-toans walk around with their eyes open while sleeping, and some move about as schools of fish.
source_quote: At this point, the escapees notice that many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: attempt to observe the Deep Father’s altar
fact: The escapees sneak to observe the altar of Leemooggoogoon but make noise, alerting the kuo-toans circling the idol and forcing a hasty retreat.
source_quote: Unfortunately, their attempt to be quiet is anything but. And the kuo-toans circling the Deep Father notice. 'I say we beat a hasty retreat,' whispers Thorin. 'These guys are spooky. Let’s get out of here,' mutters Zalthir.

subject: Gloog’s revelation of internal conflict
fact: Gloog reveals that his sister Bloppblippodd has been given too much deference, has fallen prey to madness, and that the village is divided, requiring immediate action before their support fades.
source_quote: Our society is torn to pieces by my sister Bloppblippodd. Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much. She has no respect for our ways. And she has fallen prey to this madness... Her hard-core supporters are few, but how many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown. This is why it must be dealt with now. While we still have the support of the majority.

subject: Gloog’s refusal of first strike
fact: Gloog insists that the escapees will not throw the first punch, as it would insult the honor of his father and people, and that the conflict must be resolved by the Kuo-Toans themselves.
source_quote: No, that would insult the honor of my father and our people. This is our problem, and we must resolve it.

subject: Ploop falling asleep standing
fact: After eating, Ploop falls asleep by standing up and walking outside, a behavior common to Kuo-Toans.
source_quote: After eating, Ploop falls asleep. As is the case with Kuo Toans, he stands up and walks outside.

subject: Daz covering his nose from the stench
fact: Daz, overcome by the rank smell of the Sea Mother’s altar, covers his mouth and rubs his nose with his thumb, pretending it is itchy while Ploop watches and smiles weakly.
source_quote: Meanwhile, Daz, overcome by the rank smell, has his hand over his mouth and tries to rub the smell out of his nose with his thumb. Ploop looks at him, and he smiles weakly as he pretends his nose is itchy.

subject: acceptance of Ploop’s offer
fact: The group, including Zalthir, accepts Ploop’s offer after witnessing their customs, eating cooked fish, and being reassured by Gloog’s honor-bound approach.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea... Zalthir is satisfied.

subject: Ploop’s quarters
fact: Ploop’s quarters are where the escapees stay, and where a kuo-toan named Glooglugogg speaks to them after they return from observing the Deep Father’s altar.
source_quote: Safe inside Ploop’s house, another Kuo-Toan stares at them... He says, 'My name is Glooglugogg.'

subject: huts of the kuo-toans
fact: The huts of the kuo-toans line the village, with another wall of nets at the far end, 500 feet away, and the cave wall and Darklake defining the boundaries.
source_quote: Past the walls are the huts of the kuo-toans, and at the other end of the town, almost 500 feet away, is another wall of nets.

subject: cave wall
fact: The cave wall lies to the south between the two nEttin g walls, forming a natural boundary of the village.
source_quote: Between the two walls to the south is the cave wall.

subject: village center
fact: The center of the village contains the large statue of the Sea Mother, around which four stern kuo-toa circle, alert and on guard, while others bow and chant.
source_quote: In the middle of the town is a large statue... Four stern kuo-toa slowly circle the statue, alert and on guard, while a few others move about, gazing up at the statue and bowing repeatedly while chanting.

subject: Darklake docks
fact: The Darklake docks have boats, some occupied and some empty, and are patrolled by Kuo-Toans who serve as leaders maintaining societal order.
source_quote: The Darklake side has docks. Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty. Walking along the docks are groups of Kuo-Toans. These leader types that Shuushar explained are responsible for ensuring that the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.

subject: gut-strung garlands
fact: Garlands of gut hold shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish around the neck of the Sea Mother’s statue.
source_quote: Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: dead manta ray
fact: The dead manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide on the altar of Leemooggoogoon, forming the core of the idol.
source_quote: A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide.

subject: dead octopuses
fact: Two dead octopuses are draped across the top of the Leemooggoogoon idol, their tentacles pinned and artfully arranged, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.
source_quote: Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.

subject: unidentified dried vegetable matter
fact: This material is used for ceilings in all homes in Sloobludop, and its nature remains unknown to the escapees.
source_quote: Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.

subject: Gloog’s comment on the derro
fact: Gloog remarks that the escapees did not choose to give the Kuo-Toans the derro they tied up, which he finds both honorable and odd.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: arrival of the monitor and kuo-toa delegation
fact: Twelve kuo-toa led by a monitor arrive at Ploop’s quarters to escort him, his whip, and the prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Leemooggoogoon
fact: Leemooggoogoon is the Deep Father, a deity whose existence is questioned by Zalthir, worshipped by Bloppblippodd, and whose altar is marked by a manta-ray hide idol stained with blood.
source_quote: It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists... They sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father.

subject: Sea Mother
fact: The Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess whose statue is made of wood and severed giant albino crayfish parts, and whose worship includes spitting and regurgitation as offerings.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Deep Father
fact: The Deep Father is the deity of Bloppblippodd, worshipped with a manta-ray hide idol and blood-stained altar, and is contrasted with the Sea Mother’s scavenger nature.
source_quote: The idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father... She has fallen prey to this madness.

subject: wall of nets
fact: A second wall of nets lies 500 feet from the huts, forming the eastern boundary of the village, opposite the nEttin g wall.
source_quote: At the other end of the town, almost 500 feet away, is another wall of nets.

subject: blood-stained stone altar
fact: The broad stone altar beneath the Deep Father’s idol is stained dark with blood, indicating violent ritual practices.
source_quote: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Daz shouting 'We must eat!'
fact: Daz, overwhelmed by the smell and seeking purpose, shouts 'We must eat!' prompting Ploop to reassure them that Kuo-Toans eat cooked fish.
source_quote: "We must eat!" he shouts. Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food, but Ploop, perhaps sensing that, assures him that Kuo Toans eat cooked fish.

subject: group’s acceptance of the Kuo-Toan cause
fact: The group, previously skeptical, accepts Ploop’s offer after witnessing rituals, eating cooked food, and hearing Gloog’s honorable stance on conflict resolution.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea... Zalthir is satisfied.
